note: A small primitive campground in the bottom beside Bryant Creek: a gravel lane through a mown lawn under big scattered hardwoods, with individual sites (tables and fire rings on the grass, no gravel pads) either side of it and a privy with its own small gravel lot. The creek is about 65-80 m away behind a band of bottomland timber, with a gravel bar and swimming hole downstream of the picnic area. The road in crosses Bryant Creek on a one-lane concrete low-water bridge without rails just before the campground; it goes under in high water. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' and 'Individual Campsites' - one Camping Area symbol with a privy and ADA parking on the map, one GIS point, and on imagery a real small campground (lane, lawn, about eight table/fire-ring sites, privy). Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Phone matches the area page. Pin is on the campground. Not waterfront stands. Low-water bridge on the way in - caveat written into the note.
flags: INCLUSION (stays - a built campground, not a lot): the area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites' and 'Individual Campsites'. No brochure is published. The map (9/16/2026) draws a Camping Area symbol with a Privy and ADA Parking beside it on the improved road just east of Bryant Creek, and a Picnic Area and Parking on the west bank. GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point (OBJECTID 11) at the stored pin. No horse camp is labelled.

THE SITES (0.2 m/px leaf-off frame): a gravel lane about 3-4 m wide leaves the improved road and runs about 200 m south-east through a mown lawn roughly 150 x 60 m with large scattered trees, ending at a small gravel turnaround. I count about eight small table or fire-ring features on the grass, on both sides of the lane, 20-40 m apart - that is the 'Individual Campsites'. No gravel pads or spurs are visible: rigs stand on the lane edge or the lawn. A line of posts or boulders runs along the lawn's south-west (creek-side) edge. The privy stands at the north-east side on a gravel lot about 20 x 15 m ringed with posts (GIS lot 7817, ADA). Site count is my imagery count, not a published figure, so sites.count is not written.

DISTANCE TO THE CREEK: from the lane and the nearest sites to the water of Bryant Creek is about 65-80 m (measured on the 180 m and 600 m frames), and what lies between is the post line and then a band of bottomland timber about 40-60 m deep on the bank; no road or day use between. The creek channel is about 20-25 m wide there (so 'creekside' would be the word, not riverfront). Leaf-off the water might be glimpsed through the trunks; nothing is within 50 m and I cannot show a view. Stored not waterfront stands (unsure resolves down).

ACCESS CAVEAT (low-water bridge): 'From Ava, take Highway 14 east 11 miles, then County Road 328 south 1.50 miles.' On the map the county road reaches the picnic lot on the west bank and continues as 'Improved Road' across Bryant Creek to the campground. On the 130 m frame the crossing is a concrete low-water bridge about 30 m long and one lane (about 4 m) wide, no rails, raised just above the water (it casts a shadow on the pool) with drift logs piled against its upstream side. Passable for a 23-ft rig in ordinary flow; closed by any rise. Neither the area page nor the map mentions it and no limit is posted on the page. No 4WD wording. OSM was unread (the Overpass mirror timed out). Written into the note as a caveat, as at John Alva Fuson.
